title: Bengali Chicken Shorshe Curry (Pungent Mustard Chicken)
originalTitle: Bengali Chicken Shorshe Curry (Pungent Mustard Chicken)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs bone-in or boneless chicken thighs
Shorshe Paste: 2 tbsp yellow mustard seeds + 1 tbsp black mustard seeds + 1 tbsp poppy seeds (posto), soaked in warm water 15 mins and ground with 3 green chilies and a pinch of salt
1 large onion, finely sliced or grated
1 tsp turmeric powder & 1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder
1/2 cup whisked plain yogurt, 4 slit green chilies, and fresh cilantro
instructions: Blend the soaked yellow and black mustard seeds, poppy seeds, 2 green chilies, a pinch of salt, and 1/4 cup water into a smooth mustard paste (adding salt while blending prevents bitterness).
Heat mustard oil in a wok or kadai until smoking, temper with kalonji (nigella seeds) and slit green chilies, then fry the onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, and the chicken; sear for 6–8 minutes, then stir in whisked yogurt and 3/4 cup warm water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir in the fresh mustard (shorshe) paste, simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, and finish with a raw drizzle of 1 tsp mustard oil and fresh cilantro. Serve with steamed rice.
